clue.text: Waterproof protection for military coach crashed in Midlands river

indicators.note: the word 'in' tells us the scrambled vehicle sits inside the river's name

parts.note: the Trent flows through the English Midlands

indicators.note: a coach that has crashed is wrecked, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A military coach has come off the road beside an English river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' looks like the vehicle being protected, but it is only fodder. The Trent is a major river of the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The belted raincoat was first designed for officers in the First World War trenches, hence a soldier's rainwear.

clue.text: Hood's associate in fold

definitions.meaning: Friar ... is one of Robin Hood's band of outlaws
a fold sewn into cloth, a pleat

explanation.walkthrough: Hood is Robin Hood, the English outlaw of legend; Friar Tuck was one of his Merry Men.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitched pleat in a garment is the dressmaking sense, while the friar is a legendary companion.

clue.text: Remove top of drain from which liquid may be poured

definitions.text: from which liquid may be poured

indicators.note: in a down answer the top is the first letter, and remove means drop it

parts.note: a sewer is a drain

explanation.surface: Instructions for clearing a blocked drain so water can flow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remove top of' drops the first letter, S, from SEWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A large jug with a wide spout, used for pouring water, is described by its function.

clue.text: Archaeologist astride horse, standard travel to the north for one making plans

indicators.note: astride means straddling, so the archaeologist's name sits on either side

parts.note: Howard Carter was the archaeologist who found Tutankhamun's tomb

indicators.note: in a down clue going to the north means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: par is the standard score
to go is to travel
H is slang shorthand for heroin, itself called horse

explanation.surface: An archaeologist on horseback heads north carrying a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' reverses PARGO to OGRAP; with H that sits inside CARTER, 'astride' the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A mapmaker draws plans of land, so one who makes maps is someone making plans.

clue.text: Rent taken halfway up to upper limit or bound

parts.note: a cap is a ceiling or upper limit

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read from bottom to top
taking half of a word keeps only its first part

explanation.surface: Rent has been raised halfway to its cap, or perhaps it bounds upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like the definition, but it is only fodder for the halving; 'bound' at the end is the definition, as a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a playful skip or leap, so a bound is a jump.

clue.text: Major opponent of layer within church protected by military force

indicators.note: protected by means surrounded by, so the force wraps round the rest

parts.note: an army is a military force

indicators.note: within places one piece inside another

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a hen lays eggs, so it is a layer

explanation.surface: A rival of a churchman, guarded by troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' is the egg-laying bird, not a stratum; CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A principal foe or chief adversary is the main opponent someone has.

clue.text: One beer near closing?

parts.note: one is the indefinite article a
a jar is British slang for a glass of beer

explanation.surface: A last pint ordered just before the pub shuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near closing' looks like pub closing time, but it describes a door left slightly open. A JAR is a British pub word for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A door that is slightly open is almost shut, so the question mark flags a playful description.

clue.text: Ordinary chap keeping tea-maker brews in style of 11?

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the chap's name surrounds the rest

parts.note: Joe, as in Joe Bloggs, is the everyman
an urn makes tea in quantity
ales are brews of beer

explanation.surface: An average bloke with a tea urn makes beer in the manner of a press statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is the answer to 11 Down, a press release. JOE is 'keeping' URN and ALES.
explanation.definitionFit: The clichéd prose of newspapers is a writing style typical of press announcements.

clue.text: Effect of not absorbing light or serious thought?

definitions.meaning: light bounced back from a surface instead of being taken in

explanation.definitionFit: Light that bounces off a mirror and deep musing are the physics and mental senses of the same word.

clue.text: How to get plum parts, ironically

definitions.text: How to get plum parts, ironically

parts.words: How to get plum parts, ironically
parts.note: to select only the best bits, the plum ones, you pick a different fruit entirely, which is the irony

explanation.surface: Advice on harvesting the best pieces of a plum, with a wink.
explanation.walkthrough: Plum parts are the choicest roles or bits; the verb for choosing only those is named after another fruit, hence 'ironically'.
explanation.definitionFit: Selecting only the most attractive options is the idiom, matching getting the plum parts.

clue.text: Ignore start of rant in brusque chat

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: brusque means gruff, curt in manner

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone told to skip the opening tirade during a curt conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of rant' gives R; 'Ignore' takes it out of GRUFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Guff is informal British for idle talk or nonsense, so loose chatter fits.

clue.text: Public announcement of instruction for removing seat belt?

definitions.meaning: an official statement issued to the newspapers
to undo a seat belt you push its button, the release

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase into a command: press the release catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement given to journalists is a public announcement, while a buckle's catch is unlocked by pushing it.

clue.text: Race went fast for men in show of great skill

indicators.note: putting one thing for another means substituting it in that place

parts.note: a tour de force is a feat of great skill
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers or men
ran is the past tense of run, to go fast

explanation.surface: A virtuoso performance in which someone dashed past the men.
explanation.walkthrough: In TOUR DE FORCE the OR (men, i.e. other ranks) is replaced by RAN ('went fast'), as 'for' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous cycling race around France, run each summer, is a race by name.

clue.text: Daughter enters dumbstruck, forgetting line, which leaves little time for mate

definitions.text: which leaves little time for mate

indicators.note: enters means goes in, so the daughter's letter sits inside
forgetting something means leaving it out

parts.note: someone dumbstruck is left without words

explanation.surface: A daughter walks in, leaving everyone lost for words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting' drops L from SPEECHLESS to leave SPEECHESS, and D 'enters' it. 'mate' means checkmate, not a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast chess format allows players only minutes on the clock to deliver checkmate.

clue.text: He said we move in a ring, reorganising open circus

definitions.text: He said we move in a ring

indicators.note: reorganising the words rearranges their letters

explanation.surface: A ringmaster remarks on the circus ring while reopening the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reorganising' rearranges OPEN CIRCUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polish astronomer argued that the Earth orbits the Sun, so we travel round in a circle.

clue.text: To be a breeder reactor needs work in exercise

indicators.note: 'in' places the reworked fodder within the exercise abbreviation

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: something that needs work must be reshaped, so its letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A breeder reactor, a nuclear plant type, apparently needs a workout to function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs work' rearranges REACTOR into ROCREAT, which goes 'in' PE. 'breeder reactor' is a real nuclear term, pulling the eye away from 'To be a breeder'.
explanation.definitionFit: To produce offspring is what a breeder does, so the infinitive phrase means to reproduce.

clue.text: Blemish in timber article in old museum

parts.note: ash is a timber tree
a mole is a blemish on the skin
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A flaw in wood of an item displayed in a museum.
explanation.walkthrough: The museum is the Ashmolean in Oxford, founded in 1683 and among the oldest public museums anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford institution dating from the seventeenth century is a venerable collection, hence old.

clue.text: Rent cut — cut by a penny!

indicators.note: something cut by another thing is sliced open with that thing inside it, so the coin's letter enters

parts.note: a slit is a cut
p is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A tenant's rent reduced, by exactly one penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' reads as payment to a landlord, but here it is a tear. P goes inside SLIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent is a tear or opening in fabric, the same as a crack or division.

clue.text: Check out detective in court

parts.note: a private eye is a detective
to be up before a judge is to be in court

explanation.surface: A detective surveys the courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye someone up is to look them over appraisingly, an idiom for checking someone out.

clue.text: Man fronting battle site, going as far as making revealing remark?

indicators.note: fronting means standing in front, so the male pronoun comes first

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
Ypres in Belgium was the site of several First World War battles
to, as in 'from here to there', means as far as

explanation.surface: A soldier at the front of a battlefield, pushing on to a point of disclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: YPRES is the Belgian town of First World War battles.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror's exclamation when the trick is unveiled is literally a remark that reveals, hence the question mark.

clue.text: It's too clever by half of NY, changing transport system

indicators.note: changing the letters means rearranging them
half of the two letters NY is its first letter

explanation.surface: A New Yorker rebuked for being too smart for their own good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'too clever by half' looks like the idiom, but 'half' goes with 'of NY' to give N. That joins TOO CLEVER BY and 'changing' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving belt that carries goods along a factory line is a mechanical system for moving things.

clue.text: Shade of hilltop before noon

indicators.note: before puts the hilltop ahead of the noon letter

parts.note: the brow of a hill is its top

explanation.surface: The shadow cast on a hilltop just before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shade' suggests shadow but means a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour or hue is a shade, and this earthy tint is one.

clue.text: Informally, one has to support hospital where people are busy

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece that supports another sits below it

parts.note: I've is the casual contraction of 'I have', one having

explanation.surface: Someone casually admits to propping up a hospital that is always bustling.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in I'VE is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A hive of activity is a busy place, by analogy with bees in their home.

clue.text: Rain over lake and narrow ridge

indicators.note: in a down clue the rain lying over the lake surrounds it

parts.note: rain makes things wet; as a noun, the wet is rainy weather

explanation.surface: Wet weather above a lake and a thin raised strip of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised ridge on the skin from a blow, or a seam strip on a shoe, is narrow and ridged.

clue.text: A pop star ultimately out of contact

indicators.note: out of means leaving a word, so the letter is removed from it

parts.note: to reach someone is to contact them

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the phrase

explanation.surface: A pop star who has lost touch with their fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' looks like a throwaway article but is the definition, as in 'ten pence a go'. The last letter of 'pop star', R, comes 'out of' REACH.
explanation.definitionFit: In prices such as 'two pounds a head', the article means per item, the same as apiece.

clue.text: Outwardly praise god when confining traitor one is putting down

indicators.note: outwardly points to the outside letters of the word praise
confining means enclosing, so the god's name holds the traitor and the one

parts.note: Jove is another name for Jupiter, king of the Roman gods
a rat is a traitor or informer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Praising a god while locking up a traitor who is busy belittling others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outwardly' takes P and E from 'praise'; JOVE is 'confining' RAT and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or remark that disparages someone is belittling them, an adjectival sense of putting down.

clue.text: Divine nature of saints guarding people generally

indicators.note: guarding means surrounding protectively, so the saints go round the other piece

parts.note: us stands for people in general, as in 'all of us'

explanation.surface: A meditation on the holy nature of saints watching over humanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' reads as holy, but it is the verb meaning to work out by intuition, matched by an informal British verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to discover by intuition; the informal British verb here means to work something out.

clue.text: Where all-round sportsman may compete regardless of circumstances?

definitions.meaning: an all-rounder can enter whichever contest is on offer at a sports meeting
a phrase meaning whatever happens, anyway

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: a versatile athlete may enter any of the competitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means whatever happens, so it matches regardless of what the situation turns out to be.
